components.css: .ds-refs { list-style: none; font-family: "CMU Serif", Georgia, serif; font-size: 1.075rem; line-height: 1.55; margin: 0; padding: 0; } .ds-refs li + li { margin-top: 0.55rem; } .ds-ref { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 2.4rem 1fr; align-items: baseline; column-gap: 0.35rem; color: var(--ink, #1a1a1a); text-decoration: none; } .ds-refnum { color: var(--faint, #565656); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-refname { font-style: italic; } .ds-url { font-family: "CMU Typewriter", ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 0.9em; color: var(--link, #0b3c8c); word-break: break-word; } .ds-ref:hover { text-decoration: none; } .ds-ref:hover .ds-url { text-decoration: underline; text-underline-offset: 0.18em; } .ds-ref:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--link, #0b3c8c); outline-offset: 2px; } @media (pointer: coarse), (max-width: 460px) { .ds-refs li + li { margin-top: 0; } .ds-ref { padding-block: 0.62rem; } } @media (max-width: 460px) { .ds-ref { grid-template-columns: 2rem 1fr; } }

narrative.overview:
The page is set as the artifact its audience already reads ten of a week: a single-column LaTeX article on white paper. A title block, an abstract at a narrowed measure, a numbered section, a hanging-indent bibliography, a footnote rule with a colophon under it. Nothing is a card, nothing is a button, nothing is a hero. The credibility comes from the form being genuinely the form, not a skin quoting it.

Density is a document's density, not an interface's: the whole surface is one 36rem measure centred in the viewport, roughly 856 CSS px tall on desktop, and it reads top to bottom in one pass. Depth does not exist here — a sheet of paper has no z-axis — and neither does motion, imagery or iconography. The one non-black ink is the hyperref blue, and it appears only on the seven URLs. The build refuses display scale outright: the largest type on the page is the title at 1.95rem, under twice body size.

The confirmed anti-reference is the avatar-and-button-stack every link hub ships — a round profile photo over a column of pill buttons with brand-coloured glyph icons. Also rejected, and fully deleted rather than refactored: the prior dark indigo glass / particle-network / gradient-text identity, and an intermediate two-ink risograph poster direction. Neither leaves a token behind.
keyCharacteristics: Computer Modern, self-hosted and subset — no system display face, no webfont CDN
One accent ink (hyperref blue), on URLs only
No image, no icon, no shadow, no motion, no radius
Article scale: nothing exceeds ~1.8× body size
Justified abstract, hanging-indent references, real footnote rule
Print is a first-class rendering, not an afterthought

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: The hyperref blue appears on URL text and the focus ring. It never fills, never bounds, never headlines. If a new element wants the blue, it is asking to be a link.

rules.name: The Single Surface Rule
rules.body: There is exactly one background colour on the page. Any element that needs its own background is out of world.

rules.name: The Nothing-Is-Large Rule
rules.body: No type on any surface exceeds the title's 1.95rem ceiling, and no new element may introduce a display step. Hierarchy is made with weight, centring, measure and white space — not size.

rules.name: The Two-Face Rule
rules.body: Serif for prose, typewriter for machine strings (URLs, identifiers, code). A third family is a defect.

rules.name: The Justified-Measure Rule
rules.body: Justification with hyphenation is allowed only in the abstract, and only above 460px; below that the abstract sets ragged-right, because a 30rem justify does not exist on a phone.

rules.name: The One Measure Rule
rules.body: Every element lives inside the same 36rem column. Narrowing (the abstract's 30rem) is a typographic step; widening is not available.

rules.name: The Thumb-Pads-The-Row Rule
rules.body: Touch density is bought with padding on the row, never with extra margin between rows — the printed rhythm has to survive the phone.

rules.name: The No-Z-Axis Rule
rules.body: Paper has one plane. A shadow, a lifted card, a blur or a modal overlay is out of world here regardless of how subtle it is.

rules.name: The One Rule Rule
rules.body: The page draws exactly one line: the 33%-wide (max 12rem) hairline above the colophon, the LaTeX footnote rule. Dividers, borders and underlines-as-decoration are not part of the vocabulary; the only other underline in the system is a link hover.

dos: Do keep every new element inside the single 36rem measure, and use the abstract's 30rem narrowing as the only permitted step inward.
Do set machine strings — URLs, identifiers, DOIs — in CMU Typewriter at 0.9em, spelled out in full.
Do carry new colour needs back to the six existing inks; add a token only if the page genuinely gains a register, and re-ink the dark scheme in the same commit.
Do buy touch density with block padding on the row (0.62rem) under (pointer: coarse), (max-width: 460px), leaving margins at zero.
Do re-run npm run fonts when new glyphs enter the copy — the subsets only contain printable ASCII plus a short mark set, and an unsubsetted character falls back to Georgia.
Do treat print as a shipping rendering: any new block gets a break-inside decision.
Do state a claim at body scale. This page has no promotional register to escalate into.
donts: Don't introduce a display step. The title's 1.95rem is the ceiling for every current and future surface.
Don't add a shadow, a lifted card, a blur, a gradient or a transform. There is no z-axis in this world.
Don't ship an icon, a glyph font, an avatar, or a brand logo mark — including on the link rows, where every competitor puts them.
Don't animate. No transition, no reveal-on-scroll, no motion of any kind is declared in this build, and the page is one screen tall on desktop.
Don't mask a URL behind label-only text, or replace the [n] reference numbers with bullets, dashes or icons.
Don't use the hyperref blue as a fill, a border or a heading colour.
Don't add a second background surface — no cards, no panels, no sections with their own paper.
Don't use a system font stack for anything visible; the four Computer Modern faces are the identity.
Don't justify text anywhere but the abstract, and never below 460px.
